newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Keppel FELS shares fall on poor outlook.
newsitem.headline: Keppel FELS shares fall on poor outlook.

text.p: The Share price of Keppel Corp's off-shore rigbuilding and repair unit, Keppel FELS Ltd (FELS), fell Singapore $0.50 on Tuesday morning after the company said it saw lower profits in 1997, dealers said.
After trading to a morning low at S$5.15, the shares pulled back to S$5.25 at 0355 GMT, down S$0.50 from the open. More than one million shares were traded.
"After the results yesterday when they said 1997 results would be substantially lower, we started to worry about the company," said one dealer with a local broking house.
Some analysts told Reuters after the results were announced they would revise the prospective earnings for Keppel FELS down further.

On Monday, in a statement accompanying its 1996 results, FELS reported lower contributions from its two completed floating production storage and offloading vessels (FPSOs) for Norwegian offshore group Smedvig and Norwegian national oil company, Statoil,
Analysts said their major concern was Keppel FELS' lack of new contracts and its operating margins.
"The margins they have achieved are a concern. Are the jobs they have on hand going to be profitable?" one analyst asked.
"Our greatest worry is FELS have not won any major jobs. They have actually lost some contracts to the Japanese and the Koreans," said another analyst.
